Waiting is permitted. Routes begin/end at depot 0. Output syntax:

The public C++ checker is tools/verify.cpp. It independently recomputes feasibility
and distance. Self-reported costs must agree within 0.05. The illustration above
is only syntax, not a valid solution for an example input.

and a frozen checked reference (bnv,btd), per-case raw score is:

    s = max(0, 100 - 30*max(0,nv-bnv) - 0.5*max(0,100*(td-btd)/btd))
    if nv < bnv: s += 30*(bnv-nv)
    if nv <= bnv and td < btd: s += min(30,100*(btd-td)/btd)
    s = min(s,160)

Infeasible/timeout cases score zero. Mean raw score is reported; 100 means matching
the reference, not a proof of optimality. References can be beaten. Do not read
hidden inputs, reference solutions, author assets or grader internals. Do not
hard-code instances or install external solvers. Use the standard C++17 library.

Run `python3 feedback.py` to submit the permitted source files for aggregate
feedback. It can take about one minute. The pilot uses 1 second per case; final
validation uses 3 seconds per case. The full evaluation profile uses 60 seconds
per case and a 20-minute total deadline. Respect the budget argument in all modes.
Only feedback may guide changes; final evaluation runs once after code is frozen.

You have 10 minutes to develop. Test correctness, improve the heuristic, and leave
the best code in place. Explain your changes and actual tests in your final answer.
Run feedback.py on the exact final source before finishing; do not make untested
edits after the last feedback call. A successful trajectory needs all final cases
feasible and mean raw score at least 90. Strong improvements are useful even if
that acceptance threshold is not reached.

# CVRPTW solver build script.
# Targets:
#   make            -> cvrptw_solver + tools/verify
#   make solver     -> cvrptw_solver only
#   make verify     -> tools/verify only
#   make clean      -> remove build artifacts
#   make bench      -> run tools/bench.sh on workspace/instances/public

CXX      ?= g++
CXXSTD   ?= -std=c++17

# Choose -march flag based on toolchain. Remote evaluation runs Ubuntu 22.04
# with g++ 12 and uses -march=x86-64-v3; on macOS Apple-clang we fall back to
# -march=native so 'make' still works locally.
UNAME_S := $(shell uname -s)
ifeq ($(UNAME_S),Darwin)
    MARCH ?= -march=native
else
    MARCH ?= -march=x86-64-v3
endif

OPT      ?= -O3 $(MARCH) -DNDEBUG
WARN     ?= -Wall -Wextra -Wno-unused-parameter
CXXFLAGS ?= $(CXXSTD) $(OPT) $(WARN)
LDFLAGS  ?=

SRC_SOLVER  := src/solver.cpp
SRC_VERIFY  := tools/verify.cpp

BIN_SOLVER  := cvrptw_solver
BIN_VERIFY  := tools/verify

.PHONY: all solver verify clean bench

all: solver verify

solver: $(BIN_SOLVER)

$(BIN_SOLVER): $(SRC_SOLVER) include/types.h
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -o $@ $(SRC_SOLVER) $(LDFLAGS)

verify: $(BIN_VERIFY)

$(BIN_VERIFY): $(SRC_VERIFY) include/types.h
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -o $@ $(SRC_VERIFY) $(LDFLAGS)

bench: all
	@echo "bench target is not available in the agent workspace; use tools/verify on public samples"

clean:
	rm -f $(BIN_SOLVER) $(BIN_VERIFY) out_bench.csv
	rm -rf out_*

item.text: The baseline only appends nearest customers and can stop with customers unserved when it exceeds the vehicle limit. I’ll replace it with insertion-based construction and adaptive large-neighborhood search, using cached schedules for fast feasibility checks and keeping a separate feasible incumbent.

item.text:
Replaced nearest-neighbor construction with regret insertion, destroy/repair search, annealing, and feasible 2-opt. Added cached distances and schedules, deadline handling, and best-solution retention.

Tests: `make` succeeded; all six public examples passed verification at three seconds. Final `feedback.py`: **56/56 feasible**, mean raw score **105.95**. No source changes afterward.
